title: Internal Hom from a pseudo-coherent or perfect complex to a supported complex
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. If L is in D^+_{QCoh}(O_X) and K is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], then RSheafHom(K,L) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is in D_{QCoh}(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] and is locally bounded below. If L is in D_{QCoh}(O_X) and K is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], then RSheafHom(K,L) is in D_{QCoh}(O_X). In either case, if L is supported on a closed subset T (meaning every cohomology sheaf of L restricts to zero on X\setminus T), then RSheafHom(K,L) is supported on T because derived internal Hom commutes with restriction to opens.

source.place: Tag 0A6H (Lemma quasi-coherence-internal-hom), parts (1), (2), and the support observation in Tag 0A9C proof

proof.text: For the pseudo-coherent case, the definition of pseudo-coherence gives, around every point, an open on which K is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free modules; shrinking it to an affine open U=Spec(R) inside, the finite free O_U-modules are the associated sheaves of finite free R-modules, so K|_U is the associated complex of a bounded-above complex P of finite projective R-modules. Since L is in D^+_{QCoh}(O_X), L|_U is in D_{QCoh}(O_U), so under the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] it is the associated complex of an object L' of D(R); because the associated-sheaf functor is exact and kills no nonzero module, H^i(L') is zero exactly when H^i(L|_U) is, so the cohomology of L' vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. By the restriction isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open], RSheafHom(K,L)|_U is isomorphic to RSheafHom_U(K|_U,L|_U), and the affine RHom calculation [lem-sc-affine-pseudo-coherent-rhom-qcoherent], applied to P and L', identifies this with the associated sheaf of RHom_R(P,L') and says that its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent and vanish below a bound.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, clauses (1) and (3)(a), affine reduction

proof.text: For the perfect case, K first lies in D_{QCoh}(O_X): by the definition [def-pc-perfect-complex] it is locally isomorphic to a strictly perfect complex, whose terms are direct summands of finite free modules and hence quasi-coherent, so its cohomology sheaves are locally kernels modulo images of maps of quasi-coherent modules, hence quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherence is local. Thus [lem-pc-perfect-rhom-tensor-comparison] applies to K and to M=L in D_{QCoh}(O_X), and gives a perfect dual K^vee in D_{QCoh}(O_X) and an isomorphism L tensor^L K^vee ~= RSheafHom(K,L). The derived tensor of the two objects L and K^vee of D_{QCoh}(O_X) is in D_{QCoh}(O_X) by [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-qcoh], so RSheafHom(K,L) belongs to D_{QCoh}(O_X).

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, clause (2), via the perfect tensor-Hom calculation

proof.text: Let U be any open subset of X disjoint from the closed subset T supporting L. Then every cohomology sheaf of L|_U is zero, so L|_U is the zero object of D(O_U). By the restriction isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open], RSheafHom(K,L)|_U is identified with RSheafHom(K|_U,L|_U), which is the zero object. Thus every cohomology sheaf of RSheafHom(K,L) vanishes on X minus T, so it is supported on T in both cases.

source.place: Tag 0A9C proof, support observation after the quasi-coherence lemma

proof.text: Quasi-coherence of cohomology sheaves and the assertion that the cohomology vanishes below some integer are local on X, so the affine conclusions of Step 1 assemble to the global D_{QCoh} and locally bounded-below conclusions. The perfect case is already global from Step 2, and the support conclusion is exactly the vanishing on every open disjoint from T established in Step 3.
